simple.meaning: כֵּף (kêph) is a Hebrew word meaning “a hollow rock.” BibleIQ connects the English word back to this source word so its use can be compared across Scripture.
simple.biblicalBackground: כֵּף (H3710) appears 2 times in the Hebrew Bible, beginning at Job 30:6, with occurrences in Job, Jeremiah.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to כֵּף (H3710) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: English translations can use the same English word for different Hebrew words. BibleIQ anchors the study in כֵּף (H3710) before moving outward to related references.
simple.summary: כֵּף (kêph) / H3710 is traced through Job 30:6, Jeremiah 4:29 using source-language evidence and occurrence comparison.

definitions.full: H3710. keph [ כֵּף ] noun [masculine] rock (Assyrian kâpu Dl HWB 346 ; Aramaic כֵּיפָא , perhaps Aramaic loan-word in Hebrew; √ dubious); — only plural כֵּפִים Jer 4:29 as place of refuge; Job 30:6 as dwelling-place.

occurrences.englishText: So that they dwell in frightful valleys,
Every city flees for the noise of the horsemen and archers. They go into the thickets, and climb up on the rocks. Every city is forsaken, and not a man dwells therein.
